findings.file: shared/scripts/lib/rewritability_links.py (~line 175, the `run_id = _clean(event.get("adr_id") or event.get("run_id")); if not run_id: continue` branch)
findings.finding: A `work_completed` event that names FRs in `affected_frs`/`new_frs` but carries no `adr_id`/`run_id` is skipped entirely, so a requirement whose ONLY recorded change is such an event classifies as `could_not_determine` rather than `unlinked`. That conflates "no recorded change" with "change recorded but unattributable," which the module's own three-outcome discipline says are materially different claims. The event-log reader predates this change so its guarantees are unknown here, but the module silently narrows its own "recorded changes" set.
findings.suggestion: Either skip only the run-id extraction and still record the FR as having a change with an empty run-id set (→ unlinked), or at minimum document this misclassification alongside the other named limitations in §6.

findings.finding: The regex matches `Run-ID:` anywhere in `decision_log.md` (prose, tables, fenced blocks), not only on aggregator bullets. This is disclosed in the plan doc (§5a finding 8) and empirically checked against this repo, so it is a disclosed residual — but note the regex also isn't anchored to line start, so it's slightly broader than even the plan's description ("bullet") suggests.
findings.suggestion: Consider anchoring with `^-\s\\Run-ID:\\` in MULTILINE mode, which matches the aggregator's observed output; low priority given the disclosure.

findings.finding: No test covers the preview-cap rendering (>5 unlinked ids), the `EventLogUnreadable` branch of `rewritability_detail` at the Group I wiring level, or the mixed linked+unlinked rendering. The unreadable-log branch in `group_i_rewritability.py` — the "never fails a build" guarantee's most fragile part — is only unit-tested indirectly (the shared-lib test proves propagation, but nothing proves the renderer's except-clause catches `rw.EventLogUnreadable` specifically, e.g. if `load_shared_lib` returned a module without that attribute the except would raise `AttributeError` before evaluating).
findings.suggestion: Add one Group-I-level test that monkeypatches the loaded module's `scan_fr_rationale_links` to raise `EventLogUnreadable` and asserts the "NOT EVALUATED" detail and `pass` status.

findings.finding: If `fr_ids` is empty (or every FR classifies `linked`), the "all N requirement(s)…" message fires even when N is 0 or when `unlinked`/`could_not_determine` are empty because there are no FRs at all, producing "all 0 requirement(s) with recorded changes were changed in a run that also recorded a decision-drop/ADR" — misleading phrasing for a vacuous case.
findings.suggestion: Guard the all-empty branch with `if scan.linked:` or emit a distinct "no requirements in catalog" wording.  No security issues (read-only, fixed relative paths), no regressions to existing callers (`pending_drops` is an additive wrapper; `_ADVISORY_CHECKS`/`_CHECKS` additions are backward-compatible; the updated integration test and docs correctly reflect the new I9 id).  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: approve

findings.finding: _RUN_ID_BULLET_RE` matches `Run-ID:` anywhere in `decision_log.md`, including ADR prose or fenced examples. An unrelated ADR containing `Run-ID: run-a` can make requirements changed in `run-a` appear linked, so I9 fails to report genuinely unlinked requirements.
findings.suggestion: Parse only actual Run-ID bullet lines (for example, an anchored multiline regex matching `^- Run-ID: <id>$`) and add a test containing the marker in ADR body/fenced text.  Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The advisory/pass wiring meets the “never fails a build” requirement, but this false-positive path undermines the required reporting signal.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
